text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock fell sharply over the past week—dropping nearly $48 from its November 13 close to today's $367.19—despite today's move being small. The main driver is crude oil prices, which have declined from levels that would have been around $95–100 two weeks ago to $89.53 per barrel today, squeezing refinery profit margins. Refineries run at 95.7% capacity, and while storage levels remain normal, the downward oil price trend removes the tailwind that had supported energy stocks earlier in the month.

The broader headwind is geopolitical uncertainty without a clear spark. Reports of Iranian and Houthi attacks on Saudi and Bahraini facilities early this week (November 22) haven't driven oil higher as they might have in past crises, suggesting markets are treating the risk as contained or priced in. That lack of a supply shock, combined with crude's steady decline, has weighed on refining stocks more than any single company-specific news has helped.
